inputs.source: Employee purchase request via SSO authenticated channel
Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: The only stated safeguard is an instruction to pay approved vendors, while the prompt also says payments-agent will handle remaining checks.
The prompt tells the orchestrator to rely on payments-agent for remaining checks, encouraging delegation of trust and approval context.

elements.name: Vendor quote email and attachments into orchestrator
A2A connection from orchestrator to payments-agent

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request before quote selection
controls.decay_rationale: This approval is bound only to the purchase request item and budget. It does not gate cap.delegate_payment because later quote selection and bank details are not reviewed and the approval context is not passed to payments-agent.

controls.name: Bind and propagate manager approval context to delegated payment tasks
Pin or sign payments-agent card and verify peer identity
Bind payable vendor and bank destination to approved vendor record rather than quote text
Prompt instruction to pay only vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: The prompt rule relies on the model obeying it while processing persuasive or malformed vendor quote content and while delegating trust to payments-agent.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): manager approval does not propagate to delegated payment task

attack_path.note: Trusted request starts an approved purchase workflow.
Approval occurs before quote selection and is limited to item and budget.
The orchestrator delegates payment details to payments-agent without passing approval context.
payments-agent trusts the orchestrator bearer token and pays bank details in the task.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor is low because no credited control covers this path, but the design fact that the orchestrator can authorize an irreversible delegated payment using its bearer-authenticated relationship to payments-agent, while the human approval is not bound to the final vendor or bank destination, leaves the authority-laundering path effectively unchanged from inherent risk.

forecast.watch_signal: Any product or workflow change that claims the orchestrator may approve or vary payment details itself, or any continued absence of approval context in delegated tasks, requires reassessment.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
The orchestrator chooses a quote and hands it to payments-agent to pay, while relying on payments-agent for remaining checks.

recommendations.action: Bind manager approval to the final payable vendor, amount, and bank destination, and propagate that approval context to payments-agent so delegated payments without matching approval are rejected.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted vendor quote can steer delegated payment details

attack_path.note: Quote email and attachments arrive from outside the company.
The orchestrator reads the approved vendor list but the prompt-only check does not bind bank details to a record.
The orchestrator sends chosen quote details, including bank details, to payments-agent.
payments-agent pays the bank details contained in the delegated task.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version change, longer quote-handling workflows, or prompt changes that broaden procurement scope.

evidence.observation: Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.
The orchestrator is instructed to choose the best quote, use the bank details from the chosen quote, and rely on payments-agent for remaining checks.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.

recommendations.action: Reject delegated payments unless vendor identity and bank destination are looked up from an approved vendor record rather than copied from quote text or attachments.
Add a raw-action approval gate on the final payment destination and amount, or have payments-agent require independently sourced destination confirmation before execution.

findings.title: Unverified A2A peer identity and unpinned agent card permit peer spoofing or rug pull

attack_path.note: The orchestrator depends on the peer agent card fetched at startup.
Delegated payment tasks rely on the fetched peer definition and bearer-authenticated endpoint.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor is moderate because the only credited control is a partially relevant structural approval that does not actually authenticate or pin the peer, but the design fact that the orchestrator fetches an unsigned, unpinned agent card at startup and then delegates irreversible payment tasks to a bearer-authenticated peer without identity verification leaves spoofing or rug-pull risk materially unchanged from inherent risk.

forecast.watch_signal: Agent card or peer endpoint changes, additional peer agents, or any continued use of unsigned, unpinned cards.

evidence.observation: The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
The consumed agent card specifies only bearer authentication.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token.

recommendations.action: Verify peer identity with signed agent cards or equivalent pinned definitions and reject startup or runtime changes that are not explicitly reviewed.

No runtime logs or action provenance design was provided for orchestrator actions, so attributable records cannot be assessed.
The provided design does not show external data egress from this agent other than internal delegation to payments-agent.
No loops, recursion, spend cap issues, or unbounded runtime behaviors are described in the provided artifacts.
SSO authentication is mentioned, but no request audit or nonrepudiation detail for the requester channel was provided.
The artifacts mention SSO authentication but do not describe message integrity or request channel protections in transit.
The design does not state whether the purchase request channel is encrypted or whether payloads are logged with sensitive content.
No volume, quota, or service exhaustion issues are described for the purchase request flow in the supplied artifacts.
No sender verification, signed email, or attribution controls were described for vendor quote messages.
This inbound quote flow introduces outside content, but the supplied design does not show secret disclosure on that transport itself.
No evidence in the provided design suggests quote email volume or attachments can exhaust the system.
The described delegated payment flow stays within the organization and no cross-boundary disclosure sink is specified in the artifacts.
The artifacts do not describe repeated delegation, loops, or volume conditions that would make this flow a denial-of-service path.
The assessment has no artifact about who can modify the approved vendor list or how its integrity is protected.
The vendor list is internal reference data and the supplied design does not expose it outside the trust boundary.
No availability dependency or outage behavior for the vendor list store is described in the artifacts.
No payment audit design or separation of orchestrator identity from human requester identity was provided for the peer agent.
The peer agent is only described as paying vendors; the provided design does not show it disclosing protected data.
The design excerpts do not describe loops, retries, or resource exhaustion conditions for the payment peer.
The artifacts do not state whether the A2A channel has transport encryption or whether task payloads are exposed in logs.
No protocol-level throttling, retry storms, or queueing behavior is described for this A2A connection.
The supplied design does not indicate that approval records are exposed outside authorized internal procurement participants.
No outage or lockout condition around the approval record store is described in the provided materials.

rating.rationale: Manual validation only; scripts were not runnable in this environment. Present highest inherent risk is critical because untrusted vendor quote content reaches delegated payment execution through cap.delegate_payment. Present residual remains high because the only control on that path is a behavioral prompt rule. Forecast is critical because model_upgrade or longer_task_horizon defeats that dependent control. Additional present high risk exists from unsigned, unpinned A2A peer definitions and from authority laundering where manager approval does not propagate to the peer agent.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt, agent card, and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, A2A transport configuration, payment system schema, or payment-agent runtime controls were provided, so logging, payload validation, encryption, and exact credential scope could not be verified.
No explicit approval volume or per-action review design was provided, so the manager approval was not credited as a gate on delegated payment.
